liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Eyes of the World Jam (no vocals)** (1 review): Eight-minute instrumental jam highlights the band's early tour performance style [3]
- **Candyman #1** (1 review): Energetic, uptempo take contrasts with the funeral dirge style of later years [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **Between song noodling**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Playing in the Band walkthru**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Between song noodling**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Playing in the Band #1**: back after 312 archived shows (1943 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]
- **Playing in the Band #2**: back after 312 archived shows (1943 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]
- **Between song noodling**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Eyes of the World #1 w/ vocals**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Eyes of the World #2 w/ vocals**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Supplication, Supplication [14]

## The recordings

- **gd76-05-2x.sbd.vernon.9769.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 108 min; rated 3.22/5 by 18 [1]. Said about its sound: Jams sound raw, loose, and jazzy, with Jerry blazing on guitar; Recording contains many cut sections and fragments, featuring good jazzy material [4][11]

## Around the show

- Reviewer notes missing material like the two Cassidy songs and three Attic tracks [2]
- Band prepares for touring, brushing up on standards and new material [5]
- Reviewer questions 1976 date, noting Candyman, Eyes, and Wheel were on vinyl earlier [13]
- Boston Music Hall shows two weeks later illustrate similar intro jamming techniques [3]
- Performance is relaxed and fresh, differing from the somber later versions [5]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd76-05-2x.sbd.vernon.9769.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: SBD transferred to CD; compilation of material recorded May 28, 29, and 30; Tapes via Raoul Duke, seeded to etree by Matt Vernon [1]
